title: काठमाडौँ उपत्यकाका लिच्छविकालिन बुद्धमूर्तिहरू
nepali: नेपाली इतिहासमा ईश्वी २०० देखि ८७९ सम्मको समयलाई लिच्छविकाल भनिन्छ । यस समयमा तात्कालिननेपालको आर्थिक, सामाजिक, साँस्कृतिक एवम् धार्मिक क्षेत्रमा अत्याधिक विकास भएको थियो । जस कारणलिच्छविकाललाई नेपालको ‘सुवर्ण युग’ भनिन्छ । काठमाडौँ उपत्यकामा लिच्छविकालिन बौद्ध विहारहरू, ढुङ्गेधारातथा चैत्य परिसरहरूमा विभिन्न आकार प्रकारका बुद्धमूर्तिहरू पाइन्छन् । जसमध्ये प्रस्तरका ५१ वटा तथा धातुका१२ वटा लिच्छविकालिन बुद्धमूर्तिहरूको अध्ययन गरिएको छ । प्रस्तरको ५१ वटा बुद्धमूर्तिहरूमध्ये काठमाडौँमाहेनाकर महाविहार, बाँगेमुडा, स्वयम्भू, अन्तराष्ट्रिय बौद्ध भावना केन्द्र, विक्रमशील महाविहार, चारुमति विहार,पशुपति राजराजेश्वरी घाट गरी जम्मा १७ वटा छन् । त्यसैगरी झक्तपुरको सिद्धपोखरीमा एउटा बुद्धमूर्ति छ भनेललितपुरमा ईबही स्तूप, नागबाहा, तुरणबाहा, वम्बाहा, आलोक हिति, गुईतबही, क्वन्तिबही, जेष्ठवर्ण महाविहारगरी जम्मा १८ वटा बुद्धमूर्ति पाईयो । बाँकी ३ वटा छाउनीको राष्ट्रिय संग्रहालयमा र १२ वटा चोरी भईसकेकाछन् । धातुका १२ वटा बुद्धमूर्तिहरू निजी संकलन तथा विभिन्न संग्रहालयहरूमा प्रदर्शनमा छन् ।लिच्छविकालका प्रायः बुद्धमूर्तिहरू चतुरव्यूह चैत्यमा चंक्रमण तथा भविष्य व्याकरणमुद्रामा रहेका छन् ।ललितपुरको वज्रकिर्ति महाविहारस्थित चैत्यमा वैरोचनसहित पञ्चबुद्धमूर्तिको मूर्ति र आलोकहिटि परिसरमारहेको वज्रासनमास्थित दुइ हात वरदमुद्राको बुद्धमूर्ति पनि पाइन्छ । बुद्धमूर्तिहरूमध्ये ध्वाखाबाहा, बाँगेमुढा,अन्तर्रािष्ट्रय बौद्ध भावना केन्द्र, चारुमती विहारको चतुरव्यूह चैत्यभित्रको बुद्धमूर्ति, नागबाहा र स्वयम्भूकोबुद्धमूर्ति वाहेक अन्य सबै बुद्धमूर्ति जीर्ण, अङ्गभङ्ग भएका तथा खण्डित अवस्थामा रहेका छन् । खण्डित अवस्थामारहेका बुद्धमूर्तिहरूमध्ये पशुपति राजराजेश्वरी घाटको बुद्धमूर्ति र पाटनको क्वन्तिबही अगाडिको चैत्यमा रहेकोस्वर्गावतरित बुद्धमूर्ति जिर्णोद्वार गरिएका छन् । चोरी भएका बुद्धमूर्तिहरूमध्ये पाटन भिन्छेबहाःको बुद्धमूर्ति,क्वन्तिबही अगाडिको चैत्यमा रहेको बुद्धमूर्ति र ईबही स्तूपको उत्तरपूर्वमा रहेको बुद्धमूर्ति स्थानीयहरूबाटपूनःस्थापना गरिएका छन् । चोरी भइसकेका बुद्धमूर्तिहरू स्वदेशी तथा विदेशी संग्रहालयहरूमा प्रदर्शनमा छन्भने केही बुद्धमूर्तिहरू विदेशीहरूको नीजि संकलन तथा विश्वविद्यालयहरूमा पनि रहेका छन् ।
american_english: In Nepali history, the period from 200 to 879 CE is called the Licchavi period. During this period, tremendous development occurred in the economic, social, cultural, and religious sectors of contemporary Nepal. For this reason, the Licchavi period is called the 'Golden Age' of Nepal. In the Kathmandu Valley, Buddha statues of diverse shapes and sizes are found in Licchavi-era Buddhist monasteries, stone waterspouts, and chaitya premises. Among them, 51 stone and 12 metal Buddha statues dating from the Licchavi period have been studied. Of the 51 stone Buddha statues, there are 17 in total in Kathmandu across Henakar Mahavihara, Bangemuda, Swayambhu, International Buddhist Meditation Center, Bikramashil Mahavihara, Charumati Vihara, and Pashupati Rajrajeshwari Ghat. Likewise, there is one Buddha statue at Siddhapokhari in Bhaktapur, while in Lalitpur, a total of 18 Buddha statues were found across Ibahi Stupa, Nagbaha, Turanbaha, Wambaha, Alok Hiti, Guitabahi, Kvantibahi, and Jesthavarna Mahavihara. The remaining 3 are in the National Museum at Chhauni, and 12 have been stolen. The 12 metal Buddha statues are held in private collections and displayed in various museums. Most Buddha statues of the Licchavi period in chaturvyuha chaityas are depicted in walking transit and the prophecy gesture. At the chaitya located at Vajrakirti Mahavihara in Lalitpur, a sculpture of the Five Buddhas including Vairochana is found, along with a Buddha statue seated in vajrasana with both hands in varada mudra located in the Alok Hiti complex. Among the Buddha statues, except for those at Dhwakhbaha, Bangemudha, International Buddhist Meditation Center, inside the chaturvyuha chaitya of Charumati Vihara, Nagbaha, and Swayambhu, all other Buddha statues are in dilapidated, disfigured, and broken condition. Among the broken Buddha statues, the Buddha statue at Pashupati Rajrajeshwari Ghat and the descent-from-heaven Buddha statue at the chaitya in front of Kvantibahi in Patan have been restored. Among the stolen Buddha statues, the Buddha statue of Bhinchhebaha in Patan, the Buddha statue at the chaitya in front of Kvantibahi, and the Buddha statue northeast of the Ibahi Stupa have been re-installed by local residents. The stolen Buddha statues are on exhibit in domestic and overseas museums, while several Buddha statues are also kept in the private collections of foreigners and in universities.

Across Kathmandu Valley, you come across Buddha statues of all sorts of shapes and sizes tucked away in Licchavi-era Buddhist monasteries, stone water taps, and chaitya compounds. Out of all of them, 51 stone statues and 12 metal Buddha statues dating to the Licchavi era have been studied. Of those 51 stone statues, Kathmandu has 17 in all, dotted around Henakar Mahavihara, Bangemuda, Swayambhu, the International Buddhist Meditation Centre, Bikramashil Mahavihara, Charumati Vihara, and Pashupati Rajrajeshwari Ghat. Most Licchavi-period Buddha statues inside chaturvyuha chaityas are shown strolling in cankramana and striking the bhavishya vyakarana mudra. At the chaitya in Lalitpur's Vajrakirti Mahavihara, there's a carving of the Five Buddhas including Vairochana, plus another statue sitting in vajrasana with both hands in the varada mudra over in the Alok Hiti compound.
